Going up-right leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up-left.
Going up-left would wall in number 24, the last number. So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,-1). So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would cut off the top edge (4 cells); going up-right would cut off the top edge (5 cells). So the line goes down-right.
The line must go down-left: up-right is number 21, which comes later; right is number 19, which comes later; down-right is number 16, which comes later.

The line must go up-right: up-left is number 21, which comes later.
Going left would turn number 21 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going left would turn number 23 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
